chunks.text: A pilot-scale system, consisting of a grit tank and microscreen for primary treatment followed by a SAF-MBR 2.0 for secondary treatment, was installed at the Codiga Resource Recovery Center (Stanford, CA), as illustrated in. The pilot-scale system treated municipal wastewater pumped from the Serra Street sewer on the Stanford campus for more than three years. Sewage was de-gritted in a grit tank then subject to primary treatment by screening through a 0.3 mm pore size microscreen (MS-28, Hydro International). The pilot-scale SAF-MBR 2.0 consisted of: (1) two AFBRs operated in parallel, hereafter referred to as AFBR 1 and AFBR 2, containing fluidized GAC biocarrier, and (2) a gas-sparged membrane tank equipped with ultrafiltration membranes. Recirculation of bulk fluid (twice the influent flow rate) between the three reactors enabled complete mixing and control of solids accumulation within the gas-sparged membrane tank.

chunks.text: N 2 O monitoring and field sampling experiments were conducted at a full-scale SBR located in Gockseong (GS), Korea. The GS WWTP treating approximately 4500 m 3 /day of mixed urban runoff and sanitary wastewater is equipped with flow equalization basins to prevent fluctuations in influent flow. After initial screening, wastewater in flow equalization basins is subjected to secondary treatment whereby ammonia is oxidized to nitrite or nitrate within two parallel SBRs having a total volume of 4050 m 3 (see process flow schematic described in Fig. S1 ). The two SBRs operate for approximately 32.6 h of HRT alternating between reaction and settling phases in five steps: a 5-10 min pre-mixing phase, 50-60 min reaction phase with 1500-2500 m 3 of aeration, a 5-10 min post-mixing phase, a 40-60 min of settling phase, and 30 min of decanting and filling.

chunks.text: During the denitrification process, nitrate nitrogen (NO 3 -N) in the wastewater is reduced to nitrogen gas (N 2 ) under the action of denitrifying bacteria. Denitrification is a biochemical reaction carried out by heterotrophic microbes mainly that utilize the nitrogen from nitrates (NO 3 -N) as electron acceptors and carbon sources as electron donors under conditions of extremely low dissolved oxygen. Based on practical engineering applications, when the ratio of BOD 5 to TN in the wastewater entering the denitrification process is less than 4, the addition of external carbon sources should be considered. If the ratio c(BOD 5 )/c(TN) is 4 or higher, the process of denitrification can be considered complete (Fu et al., 2022; Sun et al., 2016) . chunks.text: Water is one of the most important resources for human survival. The water demand has pronounced over the past decades due to population growth, industry development, and agricultural expansion. Although groundwater, surface water, and rainwater are conventional freshwater resources, nowadays, unconventional water resources such as wastewater are recognized as valuable resources for freshwater supply. In this regard, wastewater treatment and reuse have become viable selections for providing additional water supplies (Kim and Jang, 2006) . Membrane bioreactor (MBR) systems are one of the most promising wastewater treatment technologies growing increasingly all over the world, especially in developing countries (Wu et al., 2008) . Membrane bioreactors combine conventional activated sludge (CAS) and membrane separation technologies to produce high-quality water (Zhang et al., 2021) . MBR technology reduces plant footprint by eliminating clarifiers and conventional filters, which makes them more efficient in comparison with conventional wastewater treatment processes (Judd, 2010; Deng et al., 2015) .

chunks.text: 50 If the receiving water is impaired for nutrients, the WWTF will need additional (tertiary) treatment for their removal. Phosphorus can be removed by precipitation by either biochemical or chemical means. Even with tertiary treatment, the treated sewage may still contain pathogenic microorganisms. Therefore, disinfection is an imperative step to guarantee a microbiologically safe effluent before discharging to the aquatic ecosystems. Commonly adopted disinfection methods include chlorination using either hypochlorite or chlorine and ultraviolet treatment. Reference Design and Feasible Retrofits. In this study, the prototype of the reference municipal WWTF design is located in Ithaca, New York, with a designed capacity of 13.1 million gallon/day (MGD) and an average daily flow rate of 6.6 MGD. We note that the IAWWTF does not completely comply with the reference design because the progressive CHP system has already been in service for years. To this end, the CHP system is excluded from the reference design. Reference WWTF Design. The influent WW is first introduced into a preliminary treatment unit with screens where large solids are removed. The subsequent primary clarifier is where most of the solids are removed due to the difference in density.

The waste was made of a mix of screenings from 15-mm and 3-mm screens and was compacted in the plant. The sample was taken to the laboratory where it was homogenized and divided into 20 sub-samples of 8 kg. The procedure allowed to guarantee a good reproducibility of the sub-samples composition, which was verified analytically. The samples were stored at À18 °C. chunks.text: An equalization tank was designed to maintain airflow and homogenize the incoming  wastewater, with a maximum volume of 30,000 m 3 and a depth of 4 m. In the biological step, the MBR bioreactor, as a prominent innovation in wastewater treatment, was designed with a total membrane surface area of 4200 m 2 and a porosity of cake layer equal to 0.15 m 2 . This design facilitates the degradation of both organic and inorganic substances, reduces sludge production, and produces high-quality effluent. Moreover, the tank volume was set at 9740 m 2 , and the backwash frequency and flow rate were assumed to be 30 s and 2000 m 3 /d, respectively. Then, the RO technology was implemented to enhance and complete the wastewater treatment process. The RO membranes, characterized by their small pore size, effectively reject molecules and ions, resulting in purified water. The RO system contained four vessels with a membrane area per element of 35 m 2 /element. The assumed recovery rate for the RO system was 60 %, meaning that 60 % of the feed water was treated and converted into purified water.

chunks.text: An anaerobic membrane bioreactor (AnMBR) -a hybrid of anaerobic digestion and membrane separation -may overcome the drawbacks of the conventional anaerobic activated sludge process through the excellent sludge-water separation by a microfiltration (MF) or ultrafiltration (UF) membrane. The coupling of a membrane results in high biomass (and thus high OLR and organics removal), and produces a good quality effluent that has significantly lower amount of particles and pathogens (Liao et al., 2006) . Several recent reviews on published AnMBR studies over the past two decades show that AnMBR can achieve high COD removal (more than 85%, up to 99%) with low permeate COD (less than 100 mg/L, down to below 10 mg/L) under a range of hydraulic retention time (HRT) of 3-120 h, sludge retention time (SRT) of 15 d to infinity, volumetric OLR of 0.2-5 gCOD/L/d and operating temperature of 10-37 °C for real and/or synthetic municipal wastewater treatment (Lin et al., 2013; Ozgun et al., 2013; Skouteris et al., 2012; Smith et al., 2012; Stuckey, 2012) .
